learning: Lead has saturated near 0.07 m (60.41 at 0.07 m, 60.33 at 0.08 m). Span is the next sensing lever to test. Weights must scale with sensor x to keep the signal gain unchanged.
notes: Runs the Builder's 20 mm sensor span at lead 0.07 m, with weights scaled to 40 times x so the lateral signal gain matches the best measured controller. Only the span changes from iteration 2, so the race isolates the sensing lever.
rationale: The Builder's candidate widens the sensor row to 20 mm spacing at x = +/-0.04 and +/-0.02 m, y = 0.07 m, the best measured lead. Iterations 0-3 all ended off track at 11-16% progress with max_error 0.061-0.070 m and one line-loss event per run. Lead gains saturated: y = 0.07 m scored 60.41 and y = 0.08 m scored 60.33, with the s-bend progress flat at 0.160 across leads and drivetrains. The Builder's change is therefore the only untested sensing lever. Because the outer sensors move from 0.03 to 0.04 m, the weights must scale with x or the lateral signal gain drops. I set the weights to 40 times x, giving [1.6, 0.8, 0.0, -0.8, -1.6]. This keeps the signal per metre of offset the same as iteration 2 (1.2/0.03 = 40), so kp = 1.25 keeps its effective gain and the change isolates span. Kd 0.25, ki 0, base_speed 1.5 and last_direction are unchanged from the best measured controller (iteration 2). The 12 mm footprint at 20 mm spacing still leaves the centre reading driven by the centre sensor alone, and the tape covers the centre sensor fully, so the signal stays monotonic near centre. Expected result: fewer line-loss events and lower max_error on the oval and s-bend, more progress on all tracks, and slalom steering_oscillation near 0.15. This is a design test, not a tuned final result. Risk: a coarser row may make the signal less linear near centre, raising slalom oscillation.
